newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds finish higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds finish higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds rose across the board for the fourth consecutive day on Wednesday with dollar-linked bonds posting the biggest rise, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.07 pct to 171.62
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct to 161.75
Volume was high at 214 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds and Makams.

"The positive trend is continuing but at a much slower pace. The market rose sharply during the last month and now it is slowing down," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim. "The market will stabilise at the current level."

"Trading in the CPI-linked bonds was mixed with a positive bias. The yield on inflation-linked bonds (for one year) is now around five percent which is relatively low," said Baruch Glicksberg at Clal Insurance.

"Unlinked bonds were also mixed today. These bonds rose sharply during the last month and yields fell from 15.8 percent to 14.8 percent, which is very low. The decline reflects hopes for an interest rate cut of one percent," Glicksberg added.
"In the (unlinked) Makams we saw a little demand surplus and trading was mixed. Yields on the one-year Makam fell to 14.6 percent, which is very low," the Poalim trader said.
Traders noted that yields on the Makam reflect expectations for 1997 inflation of only nine percent, compared with approximately 11 percent this year.
Dollar-linked bonds continued to rise following the sharp rise of the U.S. currency against the shekel since Monday.
"Dollar-linked bonds still do not reflect the whole rise of the dollar. Investors do not believe the dollar will remain at its current level," Glicksberg said.

In the local foreign currency market on Wednesday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2900 shekels against 3.2720 on Tuesday. The dollar began rising on Monday against the shekel from a rate of 3.253 on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
